name: Tony Medina
_presentation_note: PROMOTED 2026-09-06 on Daniel's call, reversing the 2026-08-16 spec'ing for this artist only. He was anonymous depth behind the 'Blues Rock' format because the workbook read him and Freddy Alexander as interchangeable. That reading does not survive contact with his own material: he fronts under his own name, on his own site and his own channel, with a published catalogue of originals and a covers book you can watch him play. That is the definition of a fronted act in _players_note, so he is named and the format he stood behind retires into him. Freddy stays below as unpublished depth, which is what the face-led promise already covers.

_video_note: SWAPPED 2026-09-06, Daniel's call, and this is a hosting decision as much as a taste one. The hero was t_s2FavrDew, the Freddie King duo cut, which sits on the SIDEHATCH ARTS channel rather than Tony's. That put the most-watched thing on the page on a channel we do not control: the views accrued to someone else, and a deletion or an embed switch on their side would have blanked the top of the page with no warning. It was also the weakest footage of the five once the frames were actually compared, at 720p in a plain office space with a second player as prominent as Tony. This is the Signet copy of his Prince cover instead: 1080p, purple stage light, unmistakably him out front, and we own it. Going Down keeps its place in the footage grid as the one duo performance.
blurb: A smoky voice and a guitar played with a funk guitarist's right hand. Tony Medina plays the blues and the rock and roll that came out of it, Freddie King and B.B. King through The Cars and Prince, with a book of his own songs threaded through. He plays solo for welcome drinks and dinner, and up to a four piece when the night wants a dance floor.
seo_title: Tony Medina: blues and rock for Denver private events
meta_description: Blues and rock for private events in Denver and the Colorado mountains. Solo through four piece, fronted by Tony Medina. Send a date and we price the night.
identity: Some nights want a voice that sounds like it has been somewhere. Tony Medina sings with grit and gravel in it and plays guitar with a funk guitarist's right hand, which is why a set of blues and classic rock in his hands tends to catch a crowd that thought it had turned up for background music.

The book is the blues and most of what the blues turned into. Freddie King and B.B. King at one end, The Cars, Prince and the rock records of the seventies and nineties at the other, and his own songs threaded through. Guests recognise nearly all of it without being told what it is, which is the whole trick of a covers set at a private event.

It scales from one musician to four. Solo it is a voice and an acoustic guitar, warm enough to sit under conversation through welcome drinks and dinner. Add percussion, then bass and drums, and at the four piece it is a band with a floor in front of it.

He is a working Denver musician with his own catalogue, his own site and his own channel, so none of this has to be taken on trust. The footage on this page is his, and there is a great deal more of it where that came from.
This is a named act, published under the name of the person who fronts it, and any substitution in the lineup is named to you in advance.

ladder.bestFor: Welcome drinks, patios and dinner, at conversation volume.
Patio evenings and receptions that want a pulse under the set.
Smaller venues, and parties that want a dance floor without a full band.

He is not a listing and he is not published: `depth` renders on no surface, and this is the same unpublished availability depth he has been since 2026-08-16. The face-led promise above already covers him honestly, because it says any substitution is named to you in advance rather than pretending there is never one.
